text:
One year ago I started this company with a pitch deck, too much coffee and a lot of confidence.

By the end of year one we had $180k in revenue and a team of 4. We also had 2 failed pivots, and in month 11 we reached 17 paying customers.

The pivots are what I think about most. Both times I was sure we'd found it, and both times the market said no. They felt like failures when they happened. Now I'd call them the most expensive lessons of the year and also the most useful. Each one showed us something customers didn't need, which made it easier to see what they did need.

A few other things I learned:

Small teams move fast when everyone owns the outcome. I couldn't ask for better people than the 3 who joined me.

Revenue is honest feedback. Compliments cost nothing, and paying is a real commitment. That's why those 17 paying customers in month 11 meant more to me than any metric I could put on a slide.

Year one humbled me. In year two we'll build on what's working.

To everyone who believed in us early, thank you.
